human_tolerance.notes: A commensal gecko established in Brazil that uses buildings and other disturbed habitats; its South American populations are introduced.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: A field study of an introduced population in Valinhos, São Paulo, found reproduction throughout the year; females increased clutch frequency in the wet season.

vocalizations.description: A soft clicking or chirping heard when the animal is disturbed or near another gecko.

taxonomy.note: GBIF Backbone Taxonomy gives Squamata Gekkonidae and the authorship on the matched name; GBIF returns order Squamata for this species rather than a suborder.

external.note: GBIF usage key 5959942 and iNaturalist taxon id 68492, as matched by the GBIF backbone and the iNaturalist taxa API and given in issue #47.

common_names.note: English common name from Wikidata; Portuguese 'lagarto-de-parede' from the article's interlanguage links.

range.note: The range-wide phylogeographic study places the origin in Africa and treats all Neotropical records as the invasive H. mabouia sensu stricto lineage; BR is therefore introduced and invasive. Native country list is conservative, representing documented African range localities in this format.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia: average total length 10-12.7 cm including the tail; midpoint 0.1135 m used.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia: it eats household insect pests; diet recorded as wholly invertebrate.

traits.social.note: No open source gives a group size; geckos are territorial and mostly seen singly, so Solitary [1, 1] is judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Wikipedia describes it as nocturnal, hiding in cracks and crevices by day.

traits.defense.note: Authored: drops or flees into cover.

traits.wariness.note: Authored. Lives on and inside buildings and is unafraid of people, but quick to hide; set mid-range.

traits.body_plan.note: Quadrupedal lizard; quadruped mesh, as for the other gecko-shaped reptile in this repository.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk and Climb chosen: a wall-climbing gecko that walks on surfaces. Climb has no pose in schema/v0.1/body-plans.json, so no climb pose is declared.

traits.perching.note: Clings to walls and ceilings rather than perching on branches like a bird; set to false.

traits.nest_type.note: Judgement: lays its eggs in cracks and crevices in walls, which is a cavity site, so Cavity is the honest value.

habitat.use.note: Authored: climbs walls, trees and ceilings but also forages on the ground and around foundations, so arboreal 0.55 and ground 0.45.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: hides in cracks and crevices in walls and under debris by day, so cavity is the closest tag.

habitat.resources.note: Diet from Wikipedia; the shelter weight is judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Range-wide study describes commensalism and introduced, established New World populations.

seasonal.strategy.note: Tropical species active year round; no dormancy described.

seasonal.phases.note: The Valinhos field population reproduced year-round; wet-season females increased clutch frequency. The record does not assign a seasonal-only breeding window.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg duration is the midpoint (45 days) of the primary study incubation range, 22-68 days. Juvenile duration is omitted because the study reports maturity size rather than a fixed age.

behavior.note: Authored params for the shared ground-forager program. Climb is the declared non-walking locomotion and has no pose in schema/v0.1/body-plans.json, so no climb pose is declared; a very short flee distance matches a small animal that drops into cover. rest_sun_lo_deg/rest_sun_hi_deg set to -6/60 so the gecko rests through the warm part of the day and forages after dark.

look.note: Colours from the Wikipedia description (normally banded in black and brown, pale underside, clawed toes); proportions authored for a small gecko with a long tapering tail, and the band, eyelid and toe-pad extra parts render the banding and adhesive pads.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: No published mass range; females are on average somewhat larger than males (mean snout-vent length 54.47 mm against 51.56 mm for males), so the range is that male-to-female mean ratio applied to the 4.6 g average and rounded.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Authored geometry estimate for the required quadruped field: a small gecko carried flat on the ground and on walls, so shoulder height is set to 0.02 m, about 18% of the 0.1135 m total length. Wikipedia gives no shoulder measurement.

traits.senses.note: Authored from the species' biology: colour vision plus strong night vision for a nocturnal insectivore, with acute hearing. No open source quantifies them here.

vocalizations.click.note: Description from the Wikipedia account of the species' vocalisations; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them. No open source gives a frequency band, so freq_hz is omitted.

traits.lifespan_y.note: A low-precision simulation value for a small house gecko. The primary São Paulo reproductive study states that accurate longevity data are unavailable; this is a model parameter, not a measured lifespan.

inat.skipped: ISO 3166-2 region given without --inat-place-id; pass --inat-place-id <id> (look it up at https://www.inaturalist.org/places) to query iNaturalist for this subdivision
